subject: Server-deployed app doesn't re-read .csv file on load

messages.author: 137d83e362bdea12
messages.subject: Server-deployed app doesn't re-read .csv file on load
parts:
Hey all,

I have written and deployed an app located here: http://ctloftin.shinyapps.io/fantasy/

Basically it reads in data from a csv file and outputs it in a table. When a player is selected from the drop-down list and then the "Drafted" button is clicked, that player is removed from the list of available players in the data frame. When the page is reloaded, the data should be re-read from the csv file. However, when I do reload the page, the data is never read in again. I can access the app on one computer, draft a player, and then load on another computer, where then the player is still not included even though it's a brand-new run of the app. The only way I can get the data in it's original form is to completely terminate the app from the server and redeploy which obviously defeats the whole purpose.

This is my relevant code:

draftdata <- read.csv(file="fpprojections.csv")
shinyServer(function(input, output, clientData, session) {
}

As you can see, the data should be read in only once per visit since it is outside the shinyServer function. I have tried terminating the app from the server and redeploying to no avail. Any thoughts/suggestions would be much appreciated.

Thanks,
Colin

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: Server-deployed app doesn't re-read .csv file on load
parts:
Hi Colin,

It might help to read this part of Shiny tutorial:
http://shiny.rstudio.com/tutorial/lesson5/

especially the section on "Execution". This is from that section:

"Source scripts, load libraries, and read data sets at the beginning of server.R outside of theshinyServer function. Shiny will only run this code once, which is all you need to set your server up to run the R expressions contained in shinyServer."

According to this, your data is only read once when application is loaded and R process has started. This R process on shinyapps.io is able to serve 20 different connections. When you launch your page on a different browser or machine, it won't start a new R process; it will still re-use the same R process. Which means it will not re-read the data file. Does this make sense?

Best,
Fereshteh
